# Why are birds awesome?

- Bee Hummingbird: Cuban endemic; smallest bird in the world, 5 cm long, 1.8 g (a penny weighs 2.5 g)

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.75\linewidth]{images/behu.png}
\end{figure}  
\hfill \tiny ([*Mellisuga helenae*](https://macaulaylibrary.org/asset/89854171))


# Why are birds awesome?

- Common Ostrich: largest bird, 90 - 130kg, (~50,000 or 72,000X a Bee Hummingbird) 1.7 - 2.7m tall. Run at speeds of 43 mph for short bursts, sustained speeds of ~30 mph

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.75\linewidth]{images/coos.png}
\end{figure}  
\hfill \tiny ([*Struthio camelus*](https://macaulaylibrary.org/asset/204565301))

# Why are birds awesome?

- Peregrine Falcon: fastest flying bird, hits ~200 mph in "stoops", pulling out results in 27gs force (F-16 built to easily withstand 9gs)

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.75\linewidth]{images/pefa.png}
\end{figure}  
\hfill \tiny ([*Falco peregrinus*](https://macaulaylibrary.org/asset/288347741))


# Why are birds awesome?

- Bar-headed Goose: migrates over the Himalayans at >33,000 ft, ~4,000 ft higher than Mt. Everest.

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.75\linewidth]{images/bhgo.png}
\end{figure}  
\hfill \tiny ([*Anser indicus*](https://macaulaylibrary.org/asset/181031211))

# Why are birds important? 

1. **Scientific Importance**   
  A. Evolution   
  B. Ecology   
  C. Physiology and Neurobiology  
2. **Economic Importance**  
  A. Ecosystem Services  
  B. Recreation  
3. **Cultural Importance**  
  A. Mascots  
  B. Mythology  
  C. National Emblems  
  
# Importance to Evolutionary Biology

- Evolution by natural selection
- Allopatric speciation: Speciation in geographic isolation
- Biological species concept: Species are reproductively isolated

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = \linewidth]{images/evol.png}
\end{figure}  
\hfill \tiny (Mayr, Darwin, Peter & Rosemary Grant)

# Importance to Ecology

- Quantitative Ecology: Mathematical models for ecology
- Island Biogeography: Secies composition comes from immigration and extinction

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = \linewidth]{images/ecol1.png}
\end{figure}  
\hfill \tiny (Macarthur, Wilson) 

# Importance to Ecology

- Niche Theory: Sum of conditions a species needs to survive and reproduce
- Community Assembly: What species are where and why?

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = \linewidth]{images/ecol2.png}
\end{figure}  
\hfill \tiny (Grinnell, Diamond)

- Ethology: study of behavioral processes
